summary: A June 1963 newspaper item describes a planned 100-foot steel fire tower on Cavanal Hill near Poteau; a later trip report calls the lookout site former.

access.note: A blacktopped road leads to the summit. Whether the 1963 tower still stands is not confirmed by any source read.

visit.trail_note: 4.5-mile (7.2 km) blacktopped road to the summit; mountain-bike races and a 5-mile walk are held on the hill.

events.note: Poteau News item of June 27, 1963 says the 100-foot steel tower was scheduled for completion that week. Completion is not confirmed by a second source.

evidence.supports: 1963 item dated June 27, 1963

evidence.quote: A 100-foot steel fire tower is scheduled to be completed this week on top of the World's Highest Hill--Cavanal.

evidence.quote: Poteau city and Kerr estate donated three lots apiece for the tower site.

notes_for_editor: The tower rests on one 1963 newspaper item, transcribed on the Central US lookouts site; no source confirms completion. Its 30.5 m height is the planned height. The trip report's 'former lookout site' and the undated RadioReference entry (LeFlore County -- Cavanal Mountain) do not settle whether the steel tower stands; check with Oklahoma Forestry Services. The record name Cavanal Hill matches the official-name note (Cavanal Mountain). No corrections proposed.
